audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart was wrong on five of seven rows and contradicted the page's own whys[] text. Both layers read [Irelia, Skill, Sion, Sion, Irelia, Sion, Sion] while the packet chart reads [Sion, Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Skill, Irelia, Sion] — and every whys[] entry agrees with the packet, not with the chart. whys[0] says to concede Level 1; the chart gave it to Irelia. whys[3] says 'you bully him in any straight-line trade'; the chart gave it to Sion. whys[4] calls level 6 'genuinely two-sided'; the chart said Irelia. whys[5] calls first item 'your hardest all-in window'; the chart said Sion.
audit.why: A reader saw one answer in the chart and the opposite in the paragraph directly under it. The packet chart and the prose agree with each other and with the kits (dashless Sion cannot escape a reset chain at 4-5; Soul Furnace detonate plus Vanguard's Edge make 6 genuinely even), so the chart layer is the wrong one.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 flipped to match the packet chart, proposed as one atomic group across both layers (phases[N].side + win[N]) with ratings and phase whys moved in the same group. Ratings normalised: Irelia rows 7/10, Skill rows 5/10, Sion rows 4/10. diff stays EVEN — 50.17% over 891 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike advice was named but never timed: 'Charged = knockup. Sidestep it. Track it before every engage', 'Your committal tool', 'Your ultimate'. No cooldown number appeared anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10/9/8/7/6, Soul Furnace is 15/14/13/12/11 with a 3-second detonate window, Vanguard's Edge is 125/105/85. The whole matchup is fighting inside the Q window and after the shield pops.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t now carry Decimating Smash 10s at rank 1, Soul Furnace 15s with its 3s detonate, and Vanguard's Edge 125s. Phase whys for Levels 3, 4-5, 6 and first item now key to those windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The prose fields already handle the core interactions well (dashless Sion vs Vanguard's Edge, dodging the charge, E-stun into reset). The gaps were in the boilerplate fields: dosFull[2] is titled 'Shred with your passive' but its body was a copy of the trade line and never named Ionian Fervor or explained why shred beats health stacking; dontsFull[1] is titled 'Fight into his W shield' but its body ('Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked') describes one of your own cooldowns, not Soul Furnace; report[5] Key Ability Interactions carried no interaction at all.
audit.why: Soul Furnace is a shield that reactivates after 3 seconds for magic damage, and it grows his maximum health on kills — Riot's text. Together with Glory in Death's max-health-based damage that is the missing-interaction 'resistances-invalidated' finding: raw stat stacking is not the answer, on-hit shred is. Trading into the live shield wastes the pattern; trading after it detonates is free.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d rewritten to name Ionian Fervor's max-stack on-hit shred against his health stacking; dontsFull[1].d rewritten to the real 3-second detonate timing; report[5].t rewritten to carry the two enemy timers.
sources: champ-data/_kits sion.json W and P text

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t justified Executioner's Calling with 'his healing fights your pattern', which is vague enough to read as lane sustain. Sion has no lane heal.
audit.why: The healing is Glory in Death — the post-death zombie form's attacks heal him. That is the specific thing Grievous Wounds answers, and it is also why finishing him in a fight is not the end of the fight.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal reason re-pointed at Glory in Death in report[8].t and breakdown.late.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged 'Use Vanguard's Edge' in wants.you[2] at distance 4. That is Irelia's real R name with the two leading words of the sentence caught in the match window — a false positive, not a fabrication.

edits.after: E-stun into a Bladesurge reset the moment his charged Q is down — 10s at rank 1 — and he has no knockup to break your chain.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Decimating Smash's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your stacks build and a dashless Sion can only trade in straight lines — bait the charged Q, then E-Q him while Soul Furnace is spent.

edits.before: Vanguard’s Edge walls off his disengage and marks the kill. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sion's ultimate changes the math too.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Decimating Smash's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King plus max-stack on-hit shred out-damages his still-low armour — your hardest all-in window.

notes: The five-row chart correction is the whole story here: both layers disagreed with the packet chart AND with the page's own whys[] paragraphs, so the page rendered contradictory answers to 'who wins Level 3' and four other rows. All ten side/win edits plus the six ratings are one atomic group. Rating convention normalised to Irelia 7/10, Skill 5/10, Sion 4/10 — the file previously had Skill and Sion rows both at 4/10. The prose fields (early/mid/late/whys/spikes) were already accurate and well written and are left alone. suspectNames hit on 'Use Vanguard's Edge' is a FALSE POSITIVE. No mirror existed for sion__irelia at the time of this audit — when it is written, Level 1 must go to Sion, Levels 3 and 4-5 and first item to Irelia, Level 6 to Skill, 2+ items to Sion.
